purpose: Quick sequential backend comparison, not a complete scaling or MPI study

measurement.order: All original sizes in ascending order, then all cached sizes in ascending order; each case has three consecutive executions.
measurement.execution: One sequential process per run, no MPI and no CPU affinity pinning.
measurement.timing: GNU Time -v surrounds each executable invocation. Application phase/total times are also retained.
measurement.cache_state: Fresh process for every repetition: arithmetic caches start empty. Catalog/table allocation and filling are included in whole-workload time; caches are shared across phases within each process.
measurement.app_timer_boundary: Starts before field initialization; stops before static cache destruction. GNU Time encloses process lifetime.
measurement.summary: Timing medians are computed independently. Determinant sum is calculated per run before its median. Peak RSS is the maximum over three runs.
measurement.speedup: Ratio of original median application total to cached median application total.
measurement.rss_units: KiB in logs and CSV; MiB = KiB / 1024.
measurement.wall_time_resolution: GNU Time wall-clock text has hundredths of a second; application output reports six decimal places.

limitations: Three small matrix sizes and three runs per case on one virtualized host.
Fixed backend order; these runs do not establish performance at assignment-scale dimensions.
Later determinant phases reuse entries populated during the matrix product; these are not isolated cold determinant timings.
Backend speedup includes compact element storage and cached arithmetic together.
Compilation and full test suites were excluded from timed execution.
